metadata.name: Space Tech & Orbital Sustainability Problem Context
metadata.description: Comprehensive context data supporting the problem statement for Bit-N-Bulid
metadata.problem_statement: Space Tech & Orbital Sustainability: Build autonomous agents to track space debris, optimize satellite maneuver planning, or coordinate open-source orbital traffic management to protect global communication infrastructure.

problem_background.title: The Growing Space Debris Threat
problem_background.summary: Human activity in space has created an orbital environment with over 36,500 trackable debris objects, millions of smaller untrackable fragments, and increasing collision risk to critical communication infrastructure.
key_facts: Over 36,500 objects larger than 10cm are tracked by space surveillance networks
An estimated 1 million objects between 1-10cm exist in LEO, too small to track but large enough to disable satellites
Over 300 million objects smaller than 1cm create constant erosion risk to spacecraft surfaces
LEO (200-2000km) contains 90% of all orbital debris due to high concentration of satellites and fragmentation events
Average relative velocity in LEO collisions: 10-15 km/s (creating tremendous kinetic energy)
A 1cm object at 10km/s has kinetic energy equivalent to a small car at highway speeds

critical_fragmentation_events.description: Anti-satellite missile test destroyed Cosmos 1408 satellite at 480km altitude
critical_fragmentation_events.impact: Immediate threat to ISS, ongoing risk to Starlink and other LEO constellations
critical_fragmentation_events.orbital_decay: Slow decay at 480km, debris will remain for decades
critical_fragmentation_events.notable_incidents: ISS performed debris avoidance maneuver 1 day after the test

critical_fragmentation_events.description: First major accidental collision between two intact satellites in Earth orbit
critical_fragmentation_events.impact: Largest accidental debris cloud, created new collision risk in 780km band
critical_fragmentation_events.orbital_decay: Very slow decay, debris field will remain hazardous for 50+ years
critical_fragmentation_events.notable_incidents: Iridium satellites continue to encounter debris from this event over 15 years later

critical_fragmentation_events.description: Kinetic kill vehicle destroyed Fengyun-1C weather satellite at 865km altitude
critical_fragmentation_events.impact: Created largest debris cloud in history, significantly increased overall orbital debris density
critical_fragmentation_events.orbital_decay: At 865km, debris will persist for 100+ years
critical_fragmentation_events.notable_incidents: This single event increased trackable debris population by 25%

global_dependence.percentage_of_global_data: 40% of all data transmission involves satellites

oneweb.strategic_importance: Bridging digital divide in developing nations

globalstar.primary_uses: Asset tracking, emergency beacons, remote communications

economic_impact_of_loss.emergency_comms_loss_life_risk: Significant - remote operations depend on satellite connectivity

why_autonomous_agents_needed: Human operators cannot manually screen 600+ objects for thousands of potential conjunctions
Conjunction events can develop in minutes to hours, requiring rapid automated response
Multiple operators may propose conflicting maneuvers for the same event, requiring coordination
Global communication infrastructure operates 24/7 across time zones, demanding continuous monitoring
Manual mission planning would require 100+ human operators to match current automated capabilities

tracking.purpose: Propagate TLE orbital elements forward in time to predict satellite positions
tracking.accuracy: Within 1-2km for LEO satellites with fresh TLEs
tracking.outputs: Position and velocity vectors in ECI coordinates

conjunction_screening.approach: Compare all object pairs within screening horizon

parameters.r: Combined hard body radius (~10m for communication satellites)
parameters.σ: Position uncertainty covariance (estimated from miss distance)

maneuver_planning.approach: Generate ranked delta-v options in multiple directions
maneuver_planning.constraints: Maximum delta-v budget (typically 2 m/s per maneuver)
maneuver_planning.selection_criteria: Lowest post-maneuver Pc with minimum delta-v expenditure

multi_operator_coordination.purpose: Resolve conflicts when multiple operators propose maneuvers for same conjunction
multi_operator_coordination.conflict_rule: Lowest delta-v wins (most efficient use of fuel)
multi_operator_coordination.output: Immutable audit trail of all proposals and decisions
multi_operator_coordination.benefits: Fair resource allocation, fuel conservation, transparent decision-making

long_term_vision.goal: Preserve LEO for future generations of communication, navigation, and Earth observation services
long_term_vision.timeline: Decisions made today affect orbital environment for 50-100 years
key_principles: Active debris removal in critical bands
Open data sharing for improved conjunction assessment
Investment in improved tracking and prediction capabilities

bitnbulid_role.mission: Provide autonomous, transparent, and auditable orbital traffic management to protect global communication infrastructure
bitnbulid_role.approach: Combine SGP4 tracking, Foster/Chan probability, automated maneuver planning, and multi-operator coordination
bitnbulid_role.unique_value: Open-source orbital safety system that protects critical infrastructure while maintaining operational transparency
bitnbulid_role.alignment_with_sustainability: System enables continued safe use of LEO for all operators, preventing cascading Kessler Syndrome scenarios
